correctness.rationale: For the equilibrium renewal age A, the two independent arrays of Gaussian coordinates give (F_x,F_y)=sqrt(2DA)(M_x,M_y) in law jointly with A. Writing m and v for a standard Gaussian maximum's mean and variance, this gives rho=Delta m²/(Delta m²+EA v), with Delta=Var(sqrt(A))>0 even for deterministic resets observed at random phase. With b=Phi^{-1}(1-1/N), Mills' ratio gives b²~2 log N and b(M-b) converges to Gumbel, with second-moment convergence: the positive tail is at most exp(-z) by the normal hazard bound h(x)>=x, and the negative tail for 0<=z<=b² is at most exp(-exp(z/2)) by integrating the same bound between b-z/b and b. For z>=b² it is bounded by 2^{-N} exp[-N(z-b²)²/(2b²)], whose integrated second-moment tail tends to zero. Thus (log N)²v/m² tends to pi²/24. Integrating the equilibrium age tail gives (E sqrt A)²/EA=(8/9)(ES^{3/2})²/(ES ES²); Cauchy–Schwarz gives equality at the upper K endpoint only for constant S. The positive moment quotient cannot be zero but does approach zero for P(S=L)=L^{-7/4}, otherwise S=1, and varying the weight continuously attains every intermediate value. The Poisson coefficient and N=2 anchor follow by substitution. Canceling the common age factor in the ratio works at finite N; the normalized independent maxima differ by a standard logistic in the limit, with log N/b² tending to 1/2. Neither the age effect nor the finite-N variance is a property of independent reset clocks. Reviewed RESULT.md 5–102, VERIFICATION.md 19–23, and verify.py as text; deterministic quadrature and seeded sampling are corroboration only and were not executed. Replay is the exact tail/moment/renewal argument above.
